title: Day 1: Foundations
text:
Day 1: Monday, May 4
Theme: Foundations of Abundance Indices and Spatial Autocorrelation

08:30 - 10:00 | Session 1: Foundations of Abundance Indices

08:30 - 08:50 | Welcome & Introductions (20 min)

Ice-breaker, participant background review, and workshop logistics.

08:50 - 09:15 | Module 1: From Raw Observations to Biological Signals (25 min)

Why standardize? Isolating true abundance from noise (vessel effects, gear changes, environment).

09:15 - 10:00 | Module 2: The Evolution of Standardization Models (45 min)

The journey from GLM to GAM: handling non-linearities, random effects, and Delta-models.




10:00 - 10:15 | Morning Break ☕


10:15 - 12:00 | Session 2: Hands-on Lab 1 – Classic Frameworks

Building a robust time series from fisheries data.
Practice with mgcv and lme4 using survey and fisheries-dependent datasets.
Key task: Diagnosing fit with DHARMa and extracting standardized indices.



12:00 - 13:15 | Lunch Break 🍴


13:15 - 14:45 | Session 3: Mapping the Latent Ocean – The Spatial Engine

The Core Issue: Independence vs. Autocorrelation. Why Tobler’s Law matters for fisheries.
The Gaussian Random Field (GRF): Modeling the “invisible sheet” of spatial density.
The SPDE Approach: Solving complex spatial math using a triangulated Mesh to create continuous surfaces.



14:45 - 15:00 | Afternoon Break ☕


15:00 - 16:00 | Session 4: Hands-on Lab 2 – Spatial Scaffolding

Building the Scaffolding: Creating and testing your first Mesh in sdmTMB.
Playing with Space: Modeling spatial autocorrelation and visualizing mesh residuals.
Demo: Identifying spatial bias and “ghost” patterns in the residuals.

title: Day 2: S-T Fusion
text:
Theme: Spatio-Temporal Fusion – Adding the Fourth Dimension

08:30 - 10:00 | Session 5: Dynamics in Space and Time

Module 5: Beyond static maps—how abundance surfaces evolve.

Understanding the temporal component of fish density.

Core Concepts:

Autoregressive structures (AR1): Modelling dependencies between years.
Random Walks: Handling non-stationary trends in time.
Spatio-temporal correlations: How space and time interact.




10:15 - 12:00 | Session 6: Hands-on Lab 3 – Your First S-T Model

Fitting spatio-temporal GLMMs using sdmTMB.
Visualizing “The Movie”: Generating and comparing annual abundance surfaces to see shifts in distribution.




13:15 - 14:45 | Session 7: Advanced Spatial Structures

Anisotropy: Modelling scenarios where correlation varies by direction (e.g., along currents or bathymetric lines).
Barriers: Handling landmasses, islands, and non-navigable areas using barrier meshes.



15:00 - 16:00 | Session 8: Hands-on Lab 4 – Refining the Scaffolding

Technical Implementation: Building barrier meshes and configuring anisotropy parameters in sdmTMB.
Exercise: Comparing a standard mesh vs. a barrier mesh for a coastal dataset.

title: Day 3: VAST
text:
Theme: The VAST Framework – Deep Dive into Multivariate Ecosystems

08:30 - 10:00 | Session 9: Introduction to the VAST Architecture

Module 6: Deciphering the fit_model() function.

Understanding FieldConfig and ObsModel settings.

The Delta-Model Approach: * Linking linear predictors for encounter probability (Presence/Absence) and positive catch rates (Biomass/Abundance).



10:15 - 12:00 | Session 10: Hands-on Lab 5 – Navigating VAST

Initial Setup: Configuring the Mesh, specifying the model structure, and formatting input data for the FishStatsUtils ecosystem.
Goal: Successfully fitting a baseline VAST model.




13:15 - 14:45 | Session 11: Covariates & Catchability

Density Covariates: Incorporating environmental drivers (SST, Depth, Salinity) into the latent field.
Catchability Covariates: Standardizing for vessel power, gear types, or duration.
Random Intercepts: Implementing “Vessel-Year” effects to isolate biological signals.



15:00 - 16:00 | Session 12: Hands-on Lab 6 – Adding Complexity

Workshop Exercise: Integrating environmental environmental layers into your VAST model and interpreting the estimated effects.

title: Day 4: sdmTMB
text:
Theme: Advanced sdmTMB & Model Diagnostics

08:30 - 10:00 | Session 13: Spatially Varying Coefficients (SVC)

Module 7: Local vs. Global effects.

Modelling scenarios where the relationship between the environment and fish density changes across space.

Concept: Moving beyond a single slope for environmental drivers.



10:15 - 12:00 | Session 14: Hands-on Lab 7 – SVC and Cross-Validation

Implementation: Fitting SVC models in sdmTMB.
Model Selection: Using K-fold cross-validation to assess predictive performance and select the parsimonious model.




13:15 - 14:45 | Session 15: Validation & Uncertainty

Quantifying Trust: Calculating Confidence Intervals (CI) and the Coefficient of Variation (CV) for abundance indices.
Advanced Diagnostics: Using DHARMa for 4D spatio-temporal models to detect overdispersion, zero-inflation, and spatial outliers.



15:00 - 16:00 | Session 16: Hands-on Lab 8 – Model Comparison

The “Grand Duel”: Comparing VAST and sdmTMB outputs for the same Western ABFT dataset.
Discussing convergence issues and result interpretation.

title: Day 5: tinyVAST
text:
Theme: The tinyVAST Reconciliation & BYOP

08:30 - 10:00 | Session 17: tinyVAST – The Best of Both Worlds

Module 8: Bridging frameworks.

Why use tinyVAST? Combining the user-friendly interface of sdmTMB with the multivariate power of VAST.

Joint-Species Distributions: Simplified workflows for multi-species modeling.



10:15 - 12:00 | Session 18: Hands-on Lab 9 – The Reconciliation

Practical: Running a joint-species index standardization or a multivariate survey analysis using tinyVAST.




13:15 - 15:30 | Session 19: BYOP – Bring Your Own Data & Coaching

Individual Coaching: One-on-one support for participants’ personal research datasets.
Final Polishing: Troubleshooting convergence, exporting standardized indices, and preparing figures for publication/assessment reports.



15:30 - 16:00 | Workshop Wrap-up

Final Q&A session.
Closing remarks and Distribution of Certificates.

title: Spatiotemporal Modelling for Index Standardization
text:
📆  May 4-8, 20266
⏰  08:30–16:00 CDT
🏨  Harry Hachey Conference Center, SABS

title: Spatiotemporal Modelling for Index Standardization
text:
Learning Objectives
Through guided modules, you will learn to:

Prepare complex fisheries data for spatiotemporal analysis.
Configure models in both sdmTMB and VAST frameworks.
Interpret spatial and spatiotemporal random effects.
Diagnose model fit quality using DHARMa and other modern tools.
Hands-on Application: Apply the mastered workflows directly to your own research datasets.

title: System Setup 🤖
text: Welcome! To make the most of the Spatiotemporal Modelling Workshop, you must have your computing environment configured before we begin on Monday morning. These models (VAST, sdmTMB) are computationally intensive and rely on a specific stack of C++ compilers and spatial libraries.

title: System Setup 🤖
text:
Computing Requirements
You will need:

A laptop with administrative privileges: Necessary to install C++ compilers and Rtools.
Secondary monitor: Highly recommended so you can follow the live-coding demonstrations while keeping your own RStudio session open.
R and RStudio: Ensure you have the latest versions installed.
C++ Toolchain: Necessary for TMB (Template Model Builder) to compile the spatiotemporal models.
Git & GitHub: For collaborative code sharing and version control.

title: System Setup 🤖
text:
1. Install R and RStudio (if necessary)
We rely on recent features for spatial data handling (sf, terra). * R: Version >= 4.4.0 (4.5 recommended) - Download from cloud.r-project.org. * RStudio: Desktop version >= 2025.09 - Download from posit.co.

title: System Setup 🤖
text:
2. Install Core R Packages
Open RStudio and run this script to install the engine and the diagnostic tools.
# 1. Install CRAN dependencies
install.packages(c("devtools", "sdmTMB", "DHARMa", "sf", "terra", "ggplot2", 
                   "units", "remotes", "fmesher", "TMB", "Rcpp"))

# 2. Install VAST (and its dependency FishStatsUtils)
# VAST requires the latest development versions often found on GitHub
remotes::install_github("james-thorson/FishStatsUtils", upgrade = "always")
remotes::install_github("james-thorson/VAST", upgrade = "always")

# 3. Install tinyVAST
# The bridge between sdmTMB flexibility and VAST multivariate power
remotes::install_github("james-thorson/tinyVAST", upgrade = "always")

Verification
Run this command in your console. If it returns TRUE, your C++ compiler is working:
devtools::has_devel()

title: System Setup 🤖
text:
3. Data Preparation Checklist
To participate in the “Bring Your Own Data” sessions, please have a clean dataset ready with the following columns:

Year (Numeric integer)
Latitude / Longitude (Decimal degrees)
Response Variable (Biomass, Counts, or CPUE)
Effort (Area swept, tow duration, or number of hooks)
Vessel/Gear ID (Factor, for standardization)







Spatial Unit Warning



VAST and sdmTMB perform best when spatial coordinates are Projected (e.g., UTM in kilometers). If you only have Lat/Lon, we will cover how to project them on Day 1, but having an idea of your area’s UTM zone is a plus!

title: System Setup 🤖
text:
Troubleshooting
If you encounter errors during the installation of VAST or TMB: 1. Restart RStudio. 2. Ensure no other R sessions are running. 3. If a prompt asks “Do you want to install from sources?”, type Yes.
For urgent support, contact Sosthene AKIA via the workshop Discord channel or email. ```

title: Resources
text: The following resources provide essential documentation, tutorials, and code for mastering spatiotemporal models and index standardization in R:

title: Resources
text:
Key Packages and Documentation

tinyVAST – Multivariate Spatio-Temporal Models using Structural Equations
Advanced R package for fitting multivariate spatio-temporal models with dynamic structural equations and Gaussian Markov random fields.
Includes installation instructions, theory, and worked examples.
sdmTMB – Spatial and Spatiotemporal SPDE-Based GLMMs with TMB
Modern and user-friendly package for flexible GLMM and spatial/spatiotemporal modeling in R.
Features detailed vignettes and hands-on guides for spatial fisheries applications.
VAST – Spatio-temporal analysis of univariate or multivariate data
Official GitHub repo for the VAST package, supporting robust spatio-temporal index standardization and advanced analysis for fisheries science.

title: Resources
text:
Additional Recommended Tools

glmmTMB
Generalized linear mixed models with zero-inflation and spatial structures.
INLA and inlabru
Bayesian inference for latent Gaussian models, applicable for advanced spatial/spatiotemporal modeling.
mgcv
Comprehensive modeling package (including spatially explicit GAMs and SPDEs).


For more code samples, see each package’s documentation, vignettes, or associated preprints.
